<!-- sbx-public-files -->
## Files for the user — as an internet link
To give the user a file, put it into `/work/public/` and send the link
`https://sbx.example.test/f/anna-k3y/<file name>` as the last line of the message. Names: latin letters, no spaces.
Everything in `/work/public/` is open to anyone who has the link; never put secrets there.

<!-- sbx-sites -->
## A site on the internet: <site>-<guest>.example.test
Run a server in the sandbox on 0.0.0.0:<port> (1024–65535), then:
`curl -s -X POST http://172.31.250.1:8794/publish -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" -d '{"site":"test","port":3000}'` — the answer gives the address https://test-<guest>.example.test
(DNS and the certificate take ~1 minute). List: `GET /sites`, take down: `DELETE /publish/<site>`.
At most 3 sites. The server's owner is told about every site.

<!-- sbx-services -->
## Services: what must run without a terminal
A terminal is unloaded after 2 hours idle, and everything started from it (`&`, nohup,
tmux) dies with it. A program that must run all the time (Tailscale,
a published site's server, a bot) — make it a service:
1. A file `/work/.services/<name>.sh` (name: lower-case latin, digits, `-`, `_`). Inside:
   a command that runs in the foreground, without `&` and without daemon mode,
   e.g. `exec python3 /work/site/server.py`.
2. The keeper starts it within seconds and restarts it after a crash; output:
   `/work/.services/<name>.log`; state: `curl -s localhost:9876/status`.
3. `curl -X POST localhost:9876/stop/<name>` — stop (the file becomes `<name>.sh.off`),
   `/start/<name>` — start, `/restart/<name>` — restart. Delete the file to remove the service.
At most 10 services. When you add, stop or remove a service, tell the person in one
line: which service and why. The person sees their services with /services in Telegram.
